races.name: HKJC Worldpool Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: The one genuine pace-setter in this field; Buick's ability to control fractions from the front is the key tactical factor, though a style-fit flag notes she carries modest STYLE_FIT confidence and has posted a mixed form profile in similar going this season — her history of finding little in rear suggests front-running actually suits her better here than it might appear.
runners_data.comment: True Test tops our figures despite a lack of a win in her last five starts, a runner-up effort the standout, and she owns both today's trip and going already proven. Fit again 22 days on from stall 7 under 128lb, she's the one to beat despite that winless run.

runners_data.name: Machadadorp
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on good ground over this course and trip give Andrew Balding's filly a compelling profile; races prominently and looks ideally positioned to capitalise on a True Test-set pace, with Oisin Murphy's course craft a further asset at this venue.
runners_data.comment: Machadadorp arrives on the back of two wins in her last three starts and has both today's trip and going fully proven, yet she sits bottom of this nine on our figures. Fit again 26 days on from stall 4 under 124lb, she has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Ruby's Angel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly steps up to 7f after a win at 6f on good ground; a natural early-door type who should travel prominently, and the extra furlong on this straight track looks a logical next step, though her best form has come over shorter.
runners_data.comment: Ruby's Angel won three starts back and returns quickly, just 14 days after her latest run, with a strong speed figure and both today's trip and going proven. Her placings either side of that win have been modest, leaving a query over current form from stall 8 under 124lb.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed repeatedly in similar conditions; wears a hood, has run recently (15 days), and has strong course form at 7f on good, but will need the pace to develop ahead of her rather than the race drifting to an easy front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Shallow is winless in her last six starts, that sequence including a well-beaten ninth, and she's rated only seventh of nine here. She has, though, filled the frame regularly with two seconds and two thirds, and both today's trip and going are fully proven from stall 2 under 124lb.

runners_data.name: Planet Seeker
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 6f and has genuine speed, but as a natural prominent type pushed back in the map by the congested pace picture, Jamie Spencer will need to find a different rhythm to what this filly prefers — the redistribution is a real tactical complication here.
runners_data.comment: Planet Seeker owns the fastest speed figure of this field and sits third of nine on our assessment, having won three starts back. Her placings have since eased, third then fourth, and she has only run over today's trip, not the going, from stall 1 under 123lb.

runners_data.name: Tarot
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly has placed repeatedly at the track and handles good ground, but having missed 42 days and wearing headgear (hood), she arrives needing to rediscover form; like Planet Seeker she is naturally a pace-pressing type who is likely to find herself further back than ideal given how many quick horses populate the field.
runners_data.comment: Tarot could finish only seventh last time out. She won two starts back, after a run of placed efforts before that. Both today's trip and going are fully proven, though a 42-day absence and that below-par latest run are the concerns from stall 9 under 122lb.

runners_data.name: Havana Pusey
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 96 and the class horse in the race; Neil Callan has placed her three times at this course and trip with one win, and her hold-up profile means she is vulnerable if the pace is uncontested but very dangerous if the front-runners do unravel — the 35-day break is the only mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Havana Pusey won three starts back and has both today's trip and going fully proven, rated second of nine on solid speed figures. A below-par seventh last time is the query, but she returns fit 35 days on from stall 3 under 142lb.

runners_data.name: Song N Dance
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has won and placed at this trip and handles good ground; Tom Marquand keeps a prominent berth and the 63-day layoff is the single biggest flag, though when fresh she has run well and the form profile over 7f-8f on good is consistent.
runners_data.comment: Song N Dance has never finished worse than second in her last five starts, with two wins there, but rates only second-bottom of nine on a modest speed figure. A 63-day absence adds doubt, though she has raced over today's trip before from stall 6 under 131lb.

runners_data.name: Just A Girl
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's filly has been remarkably consistent, placing in five of her last five starts — all at 7f on good or soft — but has yet to win from hold-up; Charlie Johnston's runner is the archetype of a horse who needs a truly run race to get competitive, and whether True Test provides it is the central question.
runners_data.comment: Just A Girl has been runner-up in each of her last three starts and remains without a win in five, though a smart speed figure and quick fitness turnaround of 17 days keep her right in this from stall 5 under 131lb.

races.paceDynamic: True Test is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, William Buick should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight seven — the kind of pace that does not collapse but never becomes truly searching. Behind her, Machadadorp, Ruby's Angel and Song N Dance will push for prominent positions, while the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural spots: Planet Seeker and Tarot are genuine early-prominent horses who are likely to be shuffled back into midfield as the race map fills up ahead of them, leaving them racing in an unnatural role. Just A Girl and Havana Pusey will settle in rear and depend on a strong enough gallop to reel in the front-runners, but with only one true pace-setter the tempo may not be severe enough to set up a late swoop. This race shape most favours resolute front-to-middle types who can travel on or near the pace and sustain their effort over the final two furlongs without needing a franticly run race to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds Firm
scenarios.trigger: If True Test dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent brigade tracks without disrupting her rhythm.
scenarios.body: True Test sets a sustainable tempo that never gets away from the chasing pack but is just fast enough to drain the closers' late kick, with Buick able to manage the fractions perfectly on this straight track. Prominent types who travel smoothly just off her — Machadadorp and Ruby's Angel — are ideally placed to pounce should she weaken, keeping the advantage within the front-to-prominent group throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent War Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Machadadorp, Ruby's Angel and Song N Dance all press True Test hard from the start and the tempo escalates into a genuinely strong gallop.
scenarios.body: The battle for position raises the pace sufficiently to blunt all the front-runners over the final furlong, opening a late window for the hold-up runners arriving from off the pace. Just A Girl and Havana Pusey, both proven at this track and trip, are the chief beneficiaries if the race truly falls apart up front in the final stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Out-Of-Role Types Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Planet Seeker or Tarot overcome their redistributed positions and manage to push forward into genuine prominence, adding unexpected pressure to the lead.
scenarios.body: The pace shape becomes more contested than the map suggests, compressing the field mid-race and creating a more muddling, strung-out scenario through the final two furlongs. Horses with tactical versatility and strong finishing form on good ground, such as Ruby's Angel and Song N Dance, are best placed to exploit the chaos.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If the going proves quicker than anticipated, reducing the pace to a crawl early and prompting an unusually strong late surge.
scenarios.body: A falsely run affair in fast conditions would compress the field and see energy released late, but the hold-up horses here — Shallow, Just A Girl and Havana Pusey — face the challenge of covering ground on a straight track where there is nowhere to hide. Havana Pusey, who has won and placed at this course and trip, is the most credible beneficiary given her proven class advantage at this level.

watchPoints.text: True Test and Buick — if Buick is allowed to bowl along uncontested through the first two furlongs and the sectionals are soft, the entire race shape tilts in favour of the front-prominent group and against the closers; watch whether any prominent rival pushes up to close the gap early.

Planet Seeker and Tarot — both natural prominent types who may attempt to push forward off a slow pace despite their redistributed positions, which could disrupt True Test's rhythm and accidentally create the contested gallop the hold-up horses need.

Havana Pusey's weight — at 142lbs she carries the biggest burden in the field; on good-to-firm ground over a straight seven where pace is uncontested, the class advantage may be partially negated by the burden if the race does not truly test the front-runners.

Song N Dance — 63 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; Tom Marquand will know how ready she is, but a first-time-out bounce effect over a stiff 7f on fast ground is worth monitoring in terms of how aggressively she is ridden for position early.

Shallow's hood — the headgear worn by Shallow has coincided with her consistent placed runs, and Saffie Osborne is an apprentice claim rider; the combination of class-drop, gear and claim could flatter her market position in a race where pace dynamics are likely to suit her late style only partially.

races.name: Weatherbys Handicap

runners_data.name: Wechaad
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old has solid Good-ground form and Ryan Moore's placing instincts make him a prime candidate to slot just off the leader; five recent runs around 7-8f on similar going underpin his claims here, and he is one of the few prominent types who should find his natural position without a fight.
runners_data.comment: Wechaad is our top-rated runner of the nine, having won among his last five starts with today's trip and going both proven. Seventh last time is the obvious blot, but a strong speed figure keeps him central to the finish from stall 6 under 131lb.

runners_data.name: Sunset On Leros
runners_data.note: Marco Botti fits him with a hood and Marco Ghiani rides; his hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace quickens and creates a gap, but his best form has come at 8f on Good ground and he is capable of running into a place if the race falls apart late.
runners_data.comment: Sunset On Leros is winless in his last five starts, that sequence including a below-form eighth, though he owns a strong speed figure and both today's trip and going in his locker. He returns from stall 5 under 131lb 21 days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: St Anton
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's gelding has won two of his last four starts at 8f on Good ground and is in excellent form, but with this race holding more prominent-types than can all settle near the front, he risks being pushed wider or deeper than ideal and may not get the position that has served him so well recently.
runners_data.comment: St Anton followed back-to-back wins with a below-par effort last time, though both today's trip and going are fully proven and he's fourth of nine on our figures. Race-fit 23 days on from stall 7 under 127lb, bouncing back from that blip is the only query.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Four consecutive wins including two on Good ground at 8f underline his ability, and Saffie Osborne is an astute claimer; however, this race is stacked with horses wanting the same early position, and if he cannot assert his natural forward roll, he will be in unfamiliar tactical territory for the first time in several runs.
runners_data.comment: Wild Thoughts has won four of his last five starts, the sole blemish a runner-up effort, with both today's trip and going proven. Our figures rate him only sixth of nine on a modest speed figure, and a 42-day absence adds a fitness question from stall 4 under 125lb.

runners_data.name: Alfaraz
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides for Andrew Balding and Alfaraz comes here off a win at 8f on Good ground, but his two recent efforts over 10f look like they may have been searching for a solution that is not needed — dropping back to a sharp mile suits, though he too is a natural prominent type who may have to settle mid-pack given the field dynamics.
runners_data.comment: Alfaraz won last time out, though that follows modest efforts of fifth and sixth beforehand, and he's rated only eighth of nine despite a competitive speed figure. Proven over today's trip and going, he returns from stall 2 under 124lb needing more to threaten this line-up.

runners_data.name: Eklleem
runners_data.note: William Haggas and Tom Marquand is a powerful combination, and his last win came at 8f on Good ground, but his form at 7f suggests he appreciates being covered up; tagged as a genuine prominent type who is redistributed to midfield, he may actually handle that role better than his peers in similar circumstances.
runners_data.comment: Eklleem struck last time out, but that came after finishes of fourth, second and sixth, and he's rated bottom of this nine on a modest speed figure. He has run over today's trip before, and races from stall 1 under 123lb.

runners_data.name: Tales Of Wisdom
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's colt is the lone confirmed pace-setter and Buick will control the tempo, but his last two outings — a 28-length last and a fifth — raise legitimate questions about current form, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that even in a lead scenario he may not have the class to repel those chasing him.
runners_data.comment: Tales Of Wisdom was unplaced last time out, though that followed a win two starts back, and he owns both today's trip and going in his form book. He sits only seventh of nine on our figures, and carries 135lb from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Moonfall
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly won last time at 8f on Good ground and Billy Loughnane has been riding with confidence; she is one of the rare genuine prominent types who should secure her position naturally in this field without redistribution, making her one of the most tactically comfortable runners in the race.
runners_data.comment: Moonfall struck last time out to cap a progressive run of form, arriving with both today's trip and going already proven. Racing off an official mark of 97 that looks workable against our own assessment, he's open to further improvement under 133lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Iron Lily
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's filly has been off 68 days, which is a layoff worth monitoring, and her Good-ground form at sprint trips has been below par recently; James Doyle's experience could help her settle into a hold-up role, but she would need a more contested pace than is likely to be set here to truly threaten.
runners_data.comment: Iron Lily won three starts back and remains a leading fancy on our figures, though his last two runs, sixth then seventh, represent a downturn. A 68-day absence adds a fitness question, but he arrives with today's trip covered from stall 8 under 132lb.

races.paceDynamic: Tales Of Wisdom is the one confirmed front-runner here, and with William Buick aboard for Appleby, he is likely to set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over this straight Newmarket mile — not a scorched-earth pace, but a measured one that will suit those who travel well within themselves. The field is loaded with natural prominent types — St Anton, Wild Thoughts, Alfaraz, and Eklleem all want to race handy — but the race shape cannot accommodate all of them ahead of the main body, meaning several will be squeezed into a midfield role they do not naturally inhabit. Moonfall and Wechaad are best positioned to exploit this dynamic, as genuine prominent runners who should secure their ground without fighting for it, while the redistributed horses will either burn energy disputing or find themselves in unfamiliar territory off the pace. The tactical verdict favours prominent-to-midfield horses who settle comfortably and finish strongly on the rising ground, with the contested pace unlikely to be truly severe enough to set up a pure hold-up horse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tales Of Wisdom dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and the prominent horses directly behind him travel comfortably into the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Tales Of Wisdom sets a steady tempo that keeps the race honest without burning out the chasers, and the horses who secure the prime positions just off him — Moonfall and Wechaad — arrive with momentum to challenge before the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up, Late Closers Gain
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of natural prominent types — St Anton, Wild Thoughts, Alfaraz — do contest for position and the early fractions quicken sharply.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested early pace drains the front-runners and those who pressed them, opening a late run for horses who settled further back; Sunset On Leros and Iron Lily become more relevant if this materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is compressed and steady enough that those who do secure prominent berths — particularly the redistributed horses who manage to grab their natural position — never face a serious challenge.
scenarios.body: A stop-start or falsely run race keeps energy in the field and rewards those who hold the rail or near-side berths throughout; St Anton, with strong recent form at 8f on Good ground, is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and a gap appears down the centre of the track for a horse that has been restrained well off them.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the absence of a true tearaway gallop and the fact that genuine hold-up horses in this field are scarce; Sunset On Leros on a career-best day is the only real candidate to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Tales Of Wisdom's recent form (28th and 5th) is a serious flag — if Buick allows a soft lead, he risks capitulating in the final furlong and handing the race to whoever is sat closest behind him.

St Anton, Wild Thoughts, Alfaraz, and Eklleem are all genuine prominent types who cannot all get their preferred position — watch the first two furlongs for any crowding or jostling that burns energy before the race has truly begun.

Iron Lily's 68-day absence is the longest in this field; if she needs the run or is ring-rusty, James Doyle will have very little cover in a race where hold-up opportunities are limited by the moderate pace.

Moonfall is one of only two runners (alongside Wechaad) who should settle naturally into their correct tactical position without redistribution — their early comfort in the race could be a decisive factor in the closing stages on this straight track.

The going is officially Good to Firm for this race despite the race card listing Good — horses with a concern on fast ground should be reassessed, though no runners here carry an explicit going concern flag.

races.name: Betway Bunbury Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Colombier
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this 6yo who handles good ground fine but recent form is patchy (10th and 16th in similar company) and his OR-96 mark leaves him needing career-best; prominent style suits the expected race shape but consistency is the concern.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight of a mixed sequence that also includes an unplaced effort last time and a well-beaten 9th earlier in the campaign. Proven at today's distance and going, a rating of 102 leaves this gelding capable but up against it here.

runners_data.name: Dark Tornado
runners_data.note: Michael Wigham is in excellent form (4/5 last 14 days) and Dark Tornado bounced back to winning ways last time over this exact 7f/good combination — the hold-up style is genuine and the trainer angle is a live flag.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to break a run of modest form that included three finishes of 8th or worse beforehand. Already proven at today's distance and going, though a rating of just 97 keeps this gelding firmly in the pack rather than a leading player.

runners_data.name: The Fingal Raven
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne rides for her father Jamie; this 4yo won over 8f good and is proven at Newmarket, but the prominent style risks getting caught in traffic if the bunch off Two Tribes compresses — trainer strike rate (0/15, 14 days) is a dampener.
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back now looks some way in the past, with finishes of 5th, 5th and unplaced in the meantime. Already proven at today's distance and going, a rating of 99 keeps this gelding firmly in the pack rather than among the leading dangers here.

runners_data.name: Back In Black
runners_data.note: Fanshawe's 4yo has solid each-way form (three placings from five) and handles good ground well; a natural front-running type who is unlikely to secure his ideal position in this field, meaning he'll have to produce from slightly further back than comfortable — that positional compromise is the key risk here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but rarely far below the frame, with two runner-up efforts either side of a pair of 4ths. Proven at today's distance and going, a rating of 106 - well clear of his official mark - leaves room for more.

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore booking demands respect, and this 4yo won last time over 7f good before a summer break; paced as a hold-up horse but his recent Newmarket run (7th/7f/Stall) gives course confidence, and Moore's ability to find the winning move late makes him dangerous if fractions quicken.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back sits amid a mixed sequence that also features finishes of 8th and 7th. Proven at today's distance and going, a rating of 98 leaves this gelding capable of a place but unlikely to trouble the principals on these figures.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hannon's 5yo has placed at this level (3rd, 4th, 5th recently) and handles good ground well enough, but he is a genuinely prominent-natured horse who will find it hard to get that position with this pace-rich field — his value depends on being closer to the action than he may realistically achieve.

runners_data.name: Nostrum
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 6yo (2/23, 14 days) runs out of the hold-up position and has placed twice over 7f; a career-high difficulty at OR-90 with limited wins on good and a ten-runner positional spread that leaves him needing a clear run — interesting but hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, and the promise shown when runner-up three starts back has since faded with finishes of 5th and 8th. Proven at today's distance and going, but a rating of only 95 - tenth of thirteen - makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Aalto
runners_data.note: William Buick is a significant jockey claim for Ian Williams' stablemate of Supido; a true hold-up horse operating out of a midfield map position, Aalto won over this 7f/good combination last time and the 2yo record shows consistent placed efforts — Buick's positional awareness partially compensates for the redistributed placement.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts, though a promising 2nd last time suggests a turn in form after an unplaced run and finishes of 9th, 8th and 7th. Proven at today's distance and going, but a rating of just 94 - twelfth of thirteen - leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Physique
runners_data.note: Micky Fenton's 6yo showed decent form (1st, 2nd, 3rd in last three) and handles good ground; genuine prominent inclinations pushed into midfield by this pace-heavy field, meaning Physique will have to be produced with more patience than natural — the recent winning form is real but the positional reality is constraining.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a gradually improving sequence - 3rd, then 2nd, then a win in his last three starts. Proven at today's distance and going, though a rating of just 94 - eleventh of thirteen - leaves this gelding needing more to figure here.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: Tyler Heard partners George Margarson's 4yo who has struggled for consistency (best recent finish 4th) and whose visored form has not been strong; a true hold-up type repositioned into midfield, and the overall profile — weak trainer stats, no big-field win — does not inspire confidence at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and rated bottom of the field on our figures, though his latest effort of 4th is the best of that sequence. Proven at today's distance and going, but this gelding otherwise has plenty to find against this opposition.

runners_data.name: Royal Zabeel
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR-102 with a 5yo allowance, ridden by apprentice Conor Whiteley (5lb claim that partially offsets the burden); won over this exact 7f/good combination last time and Michael Appleby's yard has solid recent form — the highest-rated prominent horse in the field and a prominent position is achievable from his natural style.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out just seven days ago, this gelding arrives with solid recent form. Already effective at today's distance and going, the concern is that this recent upturn follows a spell of modest form beforehand.

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the confirmed pace-setter at OR-103; his 6f wins suggest the 7f may stretch stamina, but the uncontested lead is a major asset — the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that an uncontrolled leader making all is not his most natural profile, and fade in the final furlong is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures on 112 even after three unplaced efforts in a row, with the promise shown when runner-up four starts back yet to be repeated. Proven at today's distance and going already, the recent dip in placings is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Elarak
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's 4yo carries OR-103 and boasts strong Newmarket form (1st and 2nd over 7f/good), making him one of the better course-and-distance profiles in the field; Billy Loughnane rides and the prominent style slots perfectly into the expected race shape just off Two Tribes.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and already proven at today's distance and going, this gelding's rating of 112 reflects a progressive profile rather than the outright best figure in the race. A below-par 6th sits furthest back in the form, but the overall trend here is positive.

runners_data.name: Great Acclaim
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 5yo has placed four times at this level including twice at 7f/good (3rd, 2nd, 3rd in last three) — the consistency is admirable but the win has eluded him and the visor suggests he needs driving; sits naturally off the pace in a race where that position suits.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, though rarely far away with three places including a 2nd two starts back. Proven at today's distance and going, a rating of 107 puts this gelding among the leading dangers despite the lack of a win.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Jamie Spencer partners this 7yo who has a deeply uninspiring recent run of form (8-9-0-0-0-0) with zero wins or places on good over any of the last five trips; the hold-up style requires a proper pace to exploit and the overall profile, including the poor Newmarket record, makes him very hard to back.

races.paceDynamic: Two Tribes (Oisin Murphy) is the confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the front, likely controlled enough to preserve stamina reserves for those tracking close behind. Royal Zabeel, Elarak, Great Acclaim, Colombier and The Fingal Raven all have prominent tendencies and will push to sit on or near Two Tribes's girth, meaning the early order behind the leader will be competitive but not chaotic — the pace itself should be honest rather than searching. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions: Back In Black, Christian David and Physique are genuine prominent horses who are likely to find themselves racing slightly further back than ideal, with Two Tribes and Royal Zabeel best placed to own the early fore. The resulting shape — a steady-to-honest pace dictated by a single leader, with a cluster of prominent horses just off him — strongly favours runners who can sit in the first four or five and produce a sustained, grinding finish on good-to-firm ground, rather than those requiring a true end-to-end test to generate a closing run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes controls a fair pace and the horses tracking him from positions 2-5 engage in a sustained stretch duel from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Two Tribes sets an honest but measured tempo, allowing Elarak, Royal Zabeel and Great Acclaim to sit tight and unleash their finishing efforts on the rising ground; on good-to-firm turf at Newmarket's 7f, this classic stalking position rewards class and a clean draw.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Two Tribes dictates and holds
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes bowls along at a pace just slow enough that Murphy can control energy expenditure and the field cannot peg him back inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The field shapes up behind him but the absence of any horse willing to genuinely pressure him early means Two Tribes reaches the dip with a lead and enough left to repel challengers; his Newmarket form (won over 6f good) is a mild concern over this 7f trip but the easy lead mitigates that.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses late surge
scenarios.trigger: If Two Tribes overcooks it or the prominent bunch push the pace harder than expected, creating enough fractions for a well-timed late run.
scenarios.body: Dark Tornado (won last at 7f good-to-firm) and Supido (Ryan Moore, fresh off a win) are the genuine hold-up horses best-positioned to unleash a late challenge down the outside; Aalto also qualifies but is mapped out of its natural rear position, tempering expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, field bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so steady it compresses the field into a sprint finish from 2f out, favouring raw speed over tactical positioning.
scenarios.body: In this scenario prominent horses who were pushed back — particularly Physique and Christian David — are already mid-pack and disadvantaged, while the class riders (Moore, Doyle) best exploit a suddenly compressed race; Supido and Colombier can quicken from a short run.

watchPoints.text: Two Tribes (Oisin Murphy) sets the tempo — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a controlled pace, the first three or four behind him (Elarak, Royal Zabeel, Great Acclaim) will be travelling ominously into the dip, and a slow-motion collapse of those mid-pack hold-up horses becomes likely.

Dark Tornado is a live danger on the back of Michael Wigham's explosive 4/5 trainer form and a course-winning return to 7f/good — watch where Egan slots him out the back and whether he can find a clean passage from 2f out.

Back In Black, Christian David and Physique are all natural prominent horses who cannot all secure that berth — if any of them gets shuffled back past their comfort zone early and then switches wide to challenge in the straight, it risks choking off the closers behind them.

Royal Zabeel is top weight with an apprentice claim — Whiteley's 5lb saves the horse something on paper, but watch whether the combination can hold a prominent pitch under 143lbs if the bunch accelerates sharply after 4f.

Supido (Ryan Moore) warrants a tracking watch: if Moore elects to sit closer than the hold-up tag suggests, the yard's in-form record and the jockey's reading of the pace could see this horse produced earlier than anticipated, which would make him far more dangerous than his current odds may reflect.

races.name: Boodles Superlative Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Al Hudaiba
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts including a course win over seven furlongs in good going makes the trip and surface a clear positive; Charlie Appleby and William Buick represent a strong hand, though the horse is a natural prominent racer nudged into a hold-up slot because the field is overcrowded with pace, which somewhat softens its prospects if the race develops as a clean-run test.
runners_data.comment: Al Hudaiba won two of his last three starts, with proven form over today's trip and going, though an unseated exit interrupted that sequence. Racing off an official mark of 98 from stall 6 under 129lb, he sits only fifth of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Green Sovereign
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's filly posted her sole win on soft going over six furlongs and carries a concern stepping up to seven on good-to-firm; she is a confirmed prominent type who finds herself pushed into midfield by the sheer volume of pace in this field, so she will need things to fall apart in front to make her run count.
runners_data.comment: Green Sovereign won two starts back over today's trip and going, sitting well clear of his official mark of 89 on our figures. Fit again 24 days on from stall 1 under 129lb, only that below-par effort last time out gives pause.

runners_data.name: Notable Dream
runners_data.note: Unbeaten at seven furlongs in good going and trained by Marco Botti, the form profile here is genuinely compelling over course-and-distance conditions; although a natural pace-player at heart, the crowded prominent rank means he is mapped further back than ideal — his winning run at this trip in similar going is the strongest form pointer for a midfield scenario.
runners_data.comment: Notable Dream won last time out over today's trip and going but hasn't been seen for 54 days since, and he's rated bottom of this seven on our figures. Fitness following that absence is the obvious question from stall 7 under 129lb.

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner has placed twice over seven furlongs in good going and brings consistent form at this exact combination of trip and surface; sitting with his natural prominent position largely intact, he is one of the better-placed horses in the field to deliver a clean challenge if Silver Dominion weakens inside the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Pikachu boasts the sharpest speed figure of this line-up and was a close second two starts back over today's trip and going, though only fifth last time out. Yet to score in his last two starts, he remains a leading player from stall 3 under 129lb.

runners_data.name: Silver Dominion
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in this race, Oliver Cole's colt won on his only start over six furlongs on soft and now steps up in trip and class on faster ground; the uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset, though the step to seven furlongs on quicker going represents both a style opportunity and an unanswered stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Silver Dominion is unbeaten from a single start, but that was 30 days ago and his modest speed figure leaves him rated second-bottom of this seven. He does arrive with today's trip already covered, breaking from stall 2 under 129lb.

runners_data.name: Abraham Lincoln
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien on a horse who won impressively on debut over six furlongs in good going; stepping up to seven furlongs, the pedigree and stable suggest the extra furlong is manageable, and Moore's ability to position him just off the pace puts Abraham Lincoln right in the heart of the most likely winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Abraham Lincoln opened his account with authority last time and returns race-fit 15 days on, already proven over today's trip from stall 5 under 129lb. Our top-rated runner of the seven, though the profile still rests on that single start.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's runner won over seven furlongs in good going and that bare form fits the conditions here, but an OR of 85 and a tendency to be outclassed — including a twentieth-place finish — means he faces a steep hill against a field containing three OR-120 rivals; his natural style is prominent but the overcrowded front rank pushes him into a midfield berth that dulls his tactical edge.
runners_data.comment: Alfred Wallace scored two starts back and boasts both today's trip and going in his form book, though his level dipped when unplaced last time out. Breaking from stall 4 under 129lb, he remains one of the leading contenders on our figures despite that letdown.

races.paceDynamic: Silver Dominion is the confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, is set to control this race from the gates at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over Newmarket's straight seven furlongs. Abraham Lincoln and Pikachu are the most credible prominent types able to sit close behind, with the pace unlikely to be excessive given no rival is likely to challenge Silver Dominion for the lead in earnest. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader dictating a measured tempo — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently, quicken on a fast surface, and produce a clean, decisive finish; pure hold-up horses are disadvantaged as there will be no searching pace to set up a late surge. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Green Sovereign, Notable Dream, and Alfred Wallace are natural prominent racers who will be shuffled into a midfield role they do not naturally fill, with Silver Dominion and Abraham Lincoln most likely to actually secure the positions that count.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Silver Dominion Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Dominion is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, confident pace that suits his natural style.
scenarios.body: Silver Dominion dictates from the front at a controlled tempo, denying rivals a true test of stamina and making the finish a kick-for-home rather than a grind; horses able to travel prominently and quicken on fast ground are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Abraham Lincoln or Pikachu track Silver Dominion closely and produce a superior late kick to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace set by Silver Dominion is genuine enough to stretch the field but not so severe that the lead is unassailable, allowing a high-class rival travelling prominently to reel him in; Abraham Lincoln, with Ryan Moore on board from an unbeaten run, is the archetype of a horse built for exactly this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Dominion goes too fast early for the conditions and the field concertinas in the final two furlongs, giving the repositioned prominent types a late chance.
scenarios.body: Notable Dream or Green Sovereign, though racing out of their natural prominent role, could benefit if fatigue hits the front rank and a compressed finish develops; however, their redistribution to midfield means this outcome is structurally less likely than it appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a sprint finish and a lightly-raced, underrated runner catches the leaders flat-footed.
scenarios.body: Alfred Wallace's sole win came over seven furlongs in similar going and he is lightly raced enough to hold residual upside, but his redistribution into a false midfield position and modest OR of 85 makes this a low-probability outcome against classier rivals.

watchPoints.text: Silver Dominion's stamina for seven furlongs on good-to-firm is completely untested — if he fades sharply inside the two-furlong pole, Abraham Lincoln and Pikachu are positioned to capitalise immediately.
Abraham Lincoln is stepping from six furlongs on debut to a Group 2 at seven furlongs — watch the market to gauge whether O'Brien's team expects the extra furlong to suit or stretch him.

Green Sovereign, Notable Dream, and Alfred Wallace are all natural prominent racers who cannot get their preferred position — if any of them pull hard or get restless behind the pace, they risk burning energy early and weakening late.

The going report consistently shows Good to Firm at this course and distance today — any horse whose best form has come on softer ground (notably Green Sovereign, with her win on soft) carries an unresolved surface concern that could be decisive in a fast-run finish.

With only seven runners and a single pace-maker, bunching behind Silver Dominion is likely in the early stages — watch for crowding or interference at the three-furlong pole as the redistributed prominent types try to find a passage.

races.name: Al Basti Equiworld, Dubai July Cup Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: William Haggas four-year-old with four wins from seven 6f starts on Good ground and a perfect sim-going record of 4/7; Tom Marquand rides and the horse's natural prominent style means it slots straight into the prime attacking position just off Satono Reve.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and two starts back, with three wins in his last five starts and the only blemish a fall in between. Already effective at today's distance and going, and fresh enough 21 days on - a progressive colt we favour on profile alone.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: In-form with a recent Beverley win but has dropped sharply in form at this level (7th, 8th, 10th in last three); a natural prominent runner squeezed into the midfield map by the density of pace in this field, and that positional compromise is a real problem at Group 1 level.
runners_data.comment: Won four starts back but modest since, with 7th and 8th his last two efforts. Already respected at today's trip and going, and a rating of 121 keeps him firmly in the picture - though he must arrest that recent dip in form.

runners_data.name: Comanche Brave
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's charge has placed three times at the trip on Good ground but has only won once from 11 starts on similar surfaces; sits naturally up with the pace but the field's pace density will push him wider than ideal, tempering his chance.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back sits alongside a below-par 7th last time, with places in three of his last five starts overall. Proven at today's distance and going and fit after 21 days, though a rating of 114 leaves this colt needing more to figure here.

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old arrives on the back of a three-race winning streak all at 6f on Good ground, making the trip and surface beyond question; the [REDISTRIBUTED] tag means he maps to hold-up, but he is a natural prominent type who will need to find a way closer to the front than the map suggests.
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the spin catch the eye, and he arrives fit having raced over today's distance and going before. Yet a modest speed figure of 98 leaves him only ninth of eleven on our figures, making him tough to trust at this level.

runners_data.name: Prince Of India
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's gelding has had mixed recent form — a close second at the trip but also a tenth — and 49 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field; wears a tongue-tie and, as a natural prominent type displaced further back than he wants, his already moderate recent record is further pressured by positional difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, with a highest finish of 2nd sitting alongside four finishes outside the frame. Ran over today's distance and going previously, but 49 days off the track and ranked bottom of eleven on our figures leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Quinault
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' six-year-old is the closest thing to a genuine hold-up runner in the race and was 11th on his latest outing, though he won over 6f Good earlier in the season; wears headgear and has 59 days between runs, and a slow gallop — the one scenario that might bring him into play — is not the expected race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Placed form figures in three of his last five starts, including a win, but that sequence has since dipped with an unplaced effort last time out. Proven over today's distance and going, though 59 days off the track adds a query over fitness for this gelding.

runners_data.name: Satono Reve
runners_data.note: Christophe Lemaire's veteran is the only true front-runner in the race and has an immaculate record on Good ground (13/13 sim-going), but the [STYLE_FIT] flag tempers confidence slightly — he is essentially running from the front in a race where his winning form has been built around dictating solo.
runners_data.comment: Top of our figures on 124 with the fastest speed figure in this field, he's been runner-up in each of his last two starts. Already proven at today's distance and going, the challenge now is turning those places into a win, last achieved three starts back.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old has a fine recent record — wins at 6f on Good going — and Saffie Osborne takes the ride on a horse who is a natural prominent type forced wide in the map; three-year-old weight concession from the older horses is a potential factor, and a 7/7 sim-going record is compelling.
runners_data.comment: Two wins among his last five starts show ability, but that came before a below-par 8th last time out. Already raced over today's distance and going, though a rating of only 110 - tenth of eleven - makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Division
runners_data.note: William Haggas' three-year-old is tactically versatile with wins and places at 6f on Good, but the natural prominence in its style means James Doyle will have to work for position against multiple rivals with the same instinct; lightly-raced enough to improve, but this is a significant step up.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed of late, with 3rd, 2nd and 3rd his last three finishes, though his sole win in this sequence came furthest back. Proven at today's distance and going, but a modest speed figure of 95 leaves this colt needing more to figure prominently.

runners_data.name: Mission Central
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore for Aidan O'Brien on a three-year-old who has won his last four, including at 6f on Good most recently — the form stack is outstanding and the trainer-jockey combination is the strongest in the race; stepping up from 5f wins to this level and this trip is the one uncertainty, but his Good ground record (7/9) supports the surface.
runners_data.comment: Four times a winner in his last five starts, the sole blip an unplaced run four starts back - a strong sequence on paper. Already proven at today's distance and going, though a rating of just 116 leaves this gelding around midfield in this field.

runners_data.name: Venetian Sun
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has five wins from eight starts on Good or Soft ground and comes here on the back of back-to-back wins at the trip; Clifford Lee rides and the horse is weighted the lightest in the field at 125lbs, which is a tangible advantage if the race sets up as a sprint from 2f out.
runners_data.comment: Successful in each of her last two starts, with three wins from her last five outings overall, this filly arrives with solid form. Already proven at today's distance and going, though a modest speed figure of 98 is the one query against the leading pair here.

races.paceDynamic: Satono Reve is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the outset on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight 6f. The pace he sets will be honest but controlled — a lone front-runner in a Group 1 sprint typically dictates tempo on his own terms, meaning the splits will be measured enough to preserve his stamina rather than suicidal. Behind him, a cluster of natural prominent racers — Big Mojo, Comanche Brave, Division, Coppull, and Prince of India — are all competing for the same handful of positions, meaning several will be shuffled wider or deeper than they would choose, compromising their chance before a stride is run. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to a controlled pace without fighting for position: true prominent types who naturally slot in just off the leader, or horses with a high cruising speed who can quicken off a steady tempo in the final 2f, will be best placed, while the redistributed prominent types forced back into midfield will need the pace to collapse to land a blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Satono Reve Leads, Rails Rail
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve bowls along uncontested and sets a smooth, metronomic gallop that sets up a sprint for the principals from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Satono Reve dictates every yard, the tempo is honest but not brutal, and horses who can travel in second or third without fighting for space get first run — the race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f pole with the leader hard to pass. Almeraq, Mission Central, and Venetian Sun all have the pace and proximity to strike; their natural forward-running styles mean they lose no ground in the scrimmage behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind Satono Reve causes bumping, easing, and a false rhythm that sets up a late-finisher's race.
scenarios.body: Multiple prominent types checking or being checked in the first 2f would slow the overall gallop, meaning the field concertinas approaching the final furlong and raw finishing speed becomes decisive. Quinault and any hold-up runner able to pick through a compressed field benefits most, though true hold-up types are scarce in this field — most closers here are displaced prominent racers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Satono Reve pushes the tempo harder than expected and the pace tests stamina fully over the 6f trip.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop would expose any horse whose finishing effort is reliant on a false pace; horses proven on fast ground over 6f with strong recent winning form would stamp their authority in the final furlong. Double Rush's remarkable recent hat-trick at the trip and Mission Central's unbeaten 6f record give them the profile to grind out a strong-pace verdict.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a wide-open dash with no true advantage to position and the whole field arrives in a heap entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With so many prominent types compressed into midfield, a blanket finish becomes possible if the pace is perfectly even and no horse gets first run — raw RPR quality and a clear passage would be the only differentiator. Division and Coppull, both lightly-raced three-year-olds with explosive recent form, carry youth on their side if the race degenerates into a luck-in-running lottery.

watchPoints.text: Satono Reve's early fractions will set the race shape for every other runner — watch whether Lemaire pushes him on hard from the gates or seeks to preserve energy, as this single decision determines whether the pace is suicidal or controlled.

Big Mojo, Comanche Brave, Division, and Coppull will all be bidding for the same prominent positions from stalls — watch for early jostling, checking, and interference in the first furlong that could compromise multiple runners before the race has properly begun.

Mission Central's step up to 6f from his 5f wins is unproven at Group 1 level — watch whether Ryan Moore slots him in travelling comfortably in the first half or whether the extra furlong exposes a stamina question in the final stages.

Venetian Sun's 3lb weight advantage over the older horses is worth monitoring if the race degenerates into a sprint — at 125lbs she carries less than any runner in the field and that edge could prove meaningful in a tight finish.

Double Rush has never run a bad race on Good ground over 6f, but his true running style being prominent while the map places him at the rear means watch where Oisin Murphy actually positions him in the first half-furlong — if he can beg or borrow a prominent spot, his chance is live.

races.name: Debenhams Handicap

runners_data.name: Sword
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner with good-ground course form but oversubscribed prominent positions in this field mean it will likely race out of its ideal slot; the headgear flag is noted and Stuart Williams' blank 14-day record (0/18) is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Sword is winless in his last five starts, though he improved to third last time out after finishing well beaten twice previously. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, with his latest run just 29 days ago rounding off a mixed formline.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for in-form Michael Herrington (4/18 over 14 days), but Nikovo's profile shows limited good-ground winning form and five runs without a win on similar; naturally wants to race up with the pace but will be pushed back by superior rivals for that ground.
runners_data.comment: Nikovo ran creditably when third just 14 days ago and ranks second in the field on our figures. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, though he is yet to win in his last six starts and needs to go one better.

runners_data.name: Leadman
runners_data.note: Strongest course-and-distance profile in the race with multiple 7f Newmarket runs on good ground (2W4P in those conditions) and Jamie Spencer provides patient, tactical nous; though a natural prominent type fighting for space, Leadman's fitness and trip suitability make it a genuine contender across several scenarios.
runners_data.comment: Leadman won last time out and also has a runner-up effort in his last six starts. He has raced over today's trip and ground before and rates fourth on our figures; backing that up again just 21 days later is the query.

runners_data.name: Righthere Rightnow
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse — one of only two true closers in the field — and Saffie Osborne's claim is useful; connections' trainer has a solid 7/16 strike rate over 14 days, though the step up to 7f from 6f wins is the key query to resolve.
runners_data.comment: Righthere Rightnow improved to third last time out, having also managed two fourths among his last five starts, and sits third in the field on our figures. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, though he is yet to win in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Angel
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old has won twice on good ground at 7f including here at Newmarket, giving her excellent credentials for this exact race shape; the 7-lb claimer Alexandra Egan is worth noting as an unknown quantity in a potentially scrappy early race, but the form profile and course record are hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Harlequin Angel has won two of her last five starts but was unplaced last time out, having also missed the frame three starts back. She has raced over today's trip and ground before, though she rates only tenth of eleven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rogue Messiah
runners_data.note: Won on good at 6f but has yet to confirm the 7f trip suits, which is the critical question here; James Owen's stable is in fine form (9/55 over 14 days) and Daniel Muscutt is a strong booking, though the step in trip and a form blip last time add a layer of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Messiah has won two of his last five starts, including one two starts back, but was well beaten in ninth last time out. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, and needs to bounce back having been off 36 days.

runners_data.name: Secret History
runners_data.note: William Buick's presence elevates this three-year-old significantly — Ed Walker's yard has quiet but consistent form — but mapped to a hold-up position via redistribution rather than genuine style; in truth this horse wants to be closer to the pace, so any scenario requiring a wide, deep run will not flatter it.
runners_data.comment: Secret History won two of her last five starts in a row, two and three runs back, but faded to fourth last time out. She has raced over today's trip and ground before, returning here 42 days on from that below-par run.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Limited form (three runs only) but all on good ground and all placing, suggesting straightforward going and trip preferences; Charlie Johnston's runner is likely to be learning in a competitive handicap field and an unknown quantity at the top of the market is the honest read.
runners_data.comment: Glen Nevis is yet to win in his last three starts, though competitive with a third, a fourth and a second. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, but our figures rate him last of eleven, well below his official mark of 77.

runners_data.name: Crimson Spirit
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with four wins in good-ground conditions over this exact course and trip combination, top weight of 142lbs is the burden to overcome; Daniel & Claire Kubler's blank 14-day record (0/6) is minor background noise but does not override the tactical advantage of uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Spirit was only fourth last time out. He won two starts back, with a third and an unplaced run deeper in the book. He has raced over today's trip and ground before and rates the pick on our figures, with a 36-day layoff the one query.

runners_data.name: Exposure
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes a horse that has not won on turf in good ground (0/4 sim-going) but is clearly trained by John & Thady Gosden with a progressive profile; shaped to travel prominently but the going stats and a modest recent run (7th) mean it needs everything to drop right.
runners_data.comment: Exposure is winless in his last five starts, though a second four runs back shows some ability, and he has already run over today's trip, most recently 22 days ago. He races from draw 11; a below-par seventh last time is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Pinatubo's Legacy
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (only three career starts) and returning after 175 days off — the long absence is the dominant concern — though it won over this course and trip on standard Tapeta; Tom Marquand is a high-quality booking and TJ Kent has a small but active yard, but this is a horse asking questions of its fitness rather than answering them.
runners_data.comment: Pinatubo's Legacy was third last time out, having won two starts back. A lengthy 175-day absence since is the major concern for a colt near the bottom of this field on our figures, though he does have form over today's trip.

races.paceDynamic: Crimson Spirit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival pressing from the gates, should be allowed to bowl along at a controlled, honest gallop on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight seven furlongs. The field is packed with natural prominent types — Sword, Nikovo, Leadman, Harlequin Angel, Rogue Messiah, Exposure and Pinatubo's Legacy all want to race in the first half of the field — meaning several will be unable to secure their preferred position and will be shuffled wider or deeper than ideal. Crimson Spirit can therefore dictate a sustainable tempo without being ambushed, while the scrimmage behind will likely produce a compressed midfield group racing on each other's heels. This shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently without burning fuel in traffic — particularly those with the tactical speed to pick off a front-runner who controls their own rhythm — but the redistribution of so many prominent types means true hold-up horses are underrepresented, making a late swoop from deep a lower-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crimson Spirit Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Crimson Spirit leads uncontested and sets a measured, unchallenged gallop that the prominent pack cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: Crimson Spirit dictates from the front on a track and trip it has won over before, rating the race to perfection while the prominent-heavy field wastes energy fighting for position behind; Billy Loughnane, an excellent front-running partner, can time the injection of pace precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and two or three prominent horses track Crimson Spirit closely enough to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compression of so many prominent types means the sharpest of the group — those who settle best and pick up cleanly — can collar Crimson Spirit late; Harlequin Angel and Leadman, both proven over course and distance in good ground, profile as the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for position burns off the prominent runners and a horse finding a clear run from mid-division comes through on the stands rail.
scenarios.body: Sword and Nikovo, both redistributed out of their natural positions, could find themselves tracking the pace at a workable distance if the field settles; Exposure, with Ryan Moore in the saddle and proven winning form, has the class to pick off tiring rivals if the race develops right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a falsely fast early pace strings the field out and a horse held up off the bridle produces a sustained run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Secret History is the most credible beneficiary despite being redistributed to a hold-up position, given William Buick can manufacture a late run; Righthere Rightnow, a genuine hold-up type, is the only runner whose natural style truly fits this shape.

watchPoints.text: Crimson Spirit takes the lead unchallenged from the stalls — if Billy Loughnane elects to ease off the front and allow the prominent pack to bunch up, watch for Harlequin Angel or Leadman to strike decisively inside the final furlong.

The cluster of natural prominent types — Sword, Nikovo, Leadman, Rogue Messiah and Pinatubo's Legacy — will create a scrappy early phase as they compete for the same ground; any horse caught wide or checked in this melee loses its chance regardless of ability.

Pinatubo's Legacy is returning from a 175-day layoff and has only three career starts; if it shows signs of ring-rustiness or greenness early, it could cause interference to rivals racing close by — a live risk in a compact group heading down the Rowley Mile.

Exposure (Ryan Moore, Gosden) has a low sim-going win rate (0/4 on good turf) which sits at odds with its market position; watch whether Moore manoeuvres it to the stands rail for clear air, which would be the most telling sign that connections expect a forward show.

Secret History's redistribution to hold-up position masks that it genuinely wants to be closer to the pace — if William Buick attempts to ride it handy and traffic allows, it could be more dangerous than its mapped position implies.

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Melek Alreeh
runners_data.note: David Simcock's 7-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who wants cut delivered late from off a solid pace; 162 days off is a concern on fresh return, but recent form shows a win and a second at 12f on similar ground, and Daniel Muscutt rides with patience from rear.
runners_data.comment: Melek Alreeh won last time out and has been runner-up twice more in his last five starts, form that stacks up well. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, though a 162-day absence since that win is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Wonder
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 5-year-old goes on in front and is confirmed as the race's sole true front-runner; the STYLE_FIT flag indicates this role sits slightly outside its optimal pattern, but at 1m4f on good to firm it should find a comfortable rhythm without needing to burn early energy.
runners_data.comment: Wonder has been placed in all of his last five starts, including a win four back, and rates a leading threat on that profile. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, but a 75-day absence since his third last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: First Officer
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's 7-year-old has strong claims on similar going (11/15 runs, 1W4P) and is a natural prominent racer who has been displaced to midfield on the pace map because Cape Fear and Wonder are ahead of him in the queue for those positions; Sorin Moldoveanu's 7lb claim could prove significant if he can push forward.
runners_data.comment: First Officer was runner-up last time out and has also been third and fourth in his last five starts. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, is back within 30 days, and though without a win in that sequence, that readiness makes him our selection.

runners_data.name: Bintabuha
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's 4-year-old has the best trainer form (5/10, T14) in the race and Tom Marquand is a major positive, but its natural hold-up style has been bumped to midfield because more closers are present than the map can accommodate at the rear; this horse has been running mostly over 10f and the step to 1m4f is a critical unknown.
runners_data.comment: Bintabuha owns a big speed figure that hints at more capability than her bare results suggest, and she has raced over today's trip and ground before. The concern is that she has finished no better than fourth in her last five starts, with her last run 40 days ago.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3-year-old is rock solid in similar going (6/6 runs, 1W5P) and Oisin Murphy gives it a major advantage; Cape Fear genuinely wants to race prominently and has the course-and-distance profile (1/12f/GOO) to be a leading player — a lighter weight of 123lbs compared to the older horses helps significantly.
runners_data.comment: Cape Fear won last time out and has never finished worse than third in his last five starts, a genuinely progressive profile. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, but sits only sixth of six on our figures, making him hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3-year-old won last time (10 days ago) and carries positive trainer momentum (9/78, T14); Rowan Scott holds the position in the rear alongside Melek Alreeh and the horse needs a true gallop to produce its best hold-up finish — the quick turnaround is worth monitoring for freshness.
runners_data.comment: Parisian Scholar won last time out just 10 days ago, rounding off a mixed sequence that also featured a seventh and an unplaced effort further back. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, but sits only fifth of six on our figures despite that latest success.

races.paceDynamic: Wonder is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m4f at Newmarket, is likely to stride into a comfortable lead from the outset without serious pressure — creating a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a gruelling test. Cape Fear and First Officer are genuine prominent-racing types who will contest the positions just behind Wonder, meaning the early order could see a small cluster disputing the lead and near-lead berths rather than a lone front-runner with daylight. Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar are natural hold-up operators who will settle towards the rear, while Bintabuha — though a genuine hold-up type — has been mapped to midfield due to the volume of hold-up horses in this field. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all slot in naturally, with Wonder best placed to control the front and Cape Fear most likely to secure the position directly behind; the race shape that emerges — a measured gallop set by a lone leader — strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp turn of foot in the final two furlongs, provided the pace does not collapse to the point that it gifts the leader an uncontested advantage throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wonder Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Wonder dictates a fair but not scorching pace and the hold-up horses find clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: Wonder's uncontested lead sets an honest enough tempo to bring the late runners into the picture, and Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar, both with proven late kicks at this sort of trip, are positioned to sweep past a tiring pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Cape Fear Tracks, Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Wonder's gallop is honest enough and Cape Fear travels smoothly in second before striking for home early in the straight.
scenarios.body: Cape Fear's course-and-distance form is strong (1W5P in similar going) and Oisin Murphy can time a prominent run to devastating effect; tracking Wonder and quickening past in the last quarter-mile plays to Cape Fear's profile precisely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Slows, Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Wonder is allowed an entirely uncontested, dawdling pace and kicks clear from the front two furlongs out before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: A very slow tempo over 1m4f on good to firm ground would leave a well-travelled Wonder with enough petrol to hold on despite being rated just OR 82; this scenario is limited by the presence of Cape Fear and First Officer who are unlikely to allow complete stagnation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Squeeze Fails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely muddling and the hold-up horses, forced to cover extra ground wide, cannot get a clean passage in a compressed straight.
scenarios.body: Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar both need a true run to produce their best and a tactical affair with traffic in a six-runner field could see the race go to a nearer-the-pace runner who avoids the late scrimmage.

watchPoints.text: Wonder's gallop — if Arron D'Arcy (7lb claimer) sets a very slow pace, the hold-up horses Melek Alreeh and Parisian Scholar may simply not have enough race to run into, handing the race to the leader or a prominent type.

Cape Fear's position — Oisin Murphy will likely push Cape Fear to sit directly behind Wonder; if that duel for the second spot becomes a battle with First Officer, the pace could lift unexpectedly and bring the hold-up horses into play earlier than expected.

Bintabuha's trip — this horse has not run beyond 12f in recent form and Tom Marquand is stepping it up to 1m4f; if it fades in the last two furlongs after travelling well, it could interfere with the hold-up horses' runs.

Melek Alreeh's layoff — 162 days between runs is a notable fitness question for a 7-year-old; Daniel Muscutt will need to judge the pace of the race carefully from the back if the horse is not fully wound up after a long break.

Parisian Scholar's quick turnaround — only 10 days since its last run, which is a very tight schedule for a handicapper stepping up in trip; watch for any signs of staleness or underperformance relative to that recent winning effort.
